evidence.title: Examining the DOJ's effort to prosecute non-citizens accused of voting

occurrences.checkable_against: Federal election law and Department of Justice charging records
occurrences.quote_span: Most of these charges come against noncitizens who tend to be green card holders, but those people cannot vote in federal elections.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice prosecution announcements and televised press-conference records
occurrences.quote_span: Ahead of the midterm elections, the Department of Justice is leading a high-profile effort to catch and prosecute people they say illegally cast ballots, sometimes holding televised press conferences to make the announcements.
occurrences.speaker: Geoff Bennett
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice investigation and case-release records
occurrences.quote_span: They say there are hundreds more of these cases that they are investigating, and they have been releasing information on these handfuls at a time.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Federal jury verdicts in noncitizen-voting cases
occurrences.quote_span: And if they might have done that once out of a misunderstanding, it's going to be really difficult to convince a jury that they should be convicted of the crime of noncitizen voting.
occurrences.speaker: David Becker
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Federal indictments and charging documents
occurrences.quote_span: And the allegations are that they falsely claimed citizenship in order to vote.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Todd Blanche's public statement or DOJ press-conference transcript
occurrences.quote_span: Voter fraud erodes the public's trust in our electoral system, and it's vital to our democratic process that we do everything that we can to restore that trust.
occurrences.speaker: Todd Blanche, U.S. Attorney General
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Federal court case records and trial outcomes
occurrences.quote_span: It's going to be difficult for the DOJ to take some of these cases where some -- where a noncitizen might have been misled by a government employee or misunderstood what was happening and accidentally got registered, and then received something in the mail saying that they could vote and here's where to go vote.
occurrences.speaker: David Becker
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Election-fraud investigations, court findings and certified election results
occurrences.quote_span: But there is no evidence to support President Trump's claims of widespread voter fraud that skew election results.
occurrences.speaker: Geoff Bennett
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice case and prosecution records from the Biden administration
occurrences.quote_span: And they also note that they have done more on this issue so far than the Biden administration did over four years, Geoff.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice charging documents concerning ballot obstruction or destruction
occurrences.quote_span: The DOJ is also going after people who they say deliberately tried to block access to or destroy ballots,
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice indictment and charging announcements
occurrences.quote_span: Ali Rogin: Yes, so far, they have announced indictments or charges of voter fraud against about 100 individuals.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice charging announcements involving Minnesota
occurrences.quote_span: So, last week, it was 10 individuals out of Minnesota.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice case records and certified election results
occurrences.quote_span: Even though the DOJ is stepping up the scope and the tempo of these allegations and of the charges, they don't amount to anything close to the widespread voter interference that would actually change the election results.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice charging announcements from the named states
occurrences.quote_span: This week, so far it's been six from a number of states.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice charging records and federal court conviction records
occurrences.quote_span: Well, so far, our own review shows that they are announcing far more charges than they are convictions.
occurrences.speaker: Ali Rogin
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: DOJ spokesperson statement and state and local election ballot records
occurrences.quote_span: But a DOJ spokesperson tells me, Geoff, that each vote that is cast illegally cancels out an American citizens' vote, and that federal races often share the ballot with downballot races for state and local candidates, where the margins are sometimes much closer.
occurrences.speaker: DOJ spokesperson
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice

occurrences.checkable_against: Department of Justice charging records and federal court conviction records
occurrences.quote_span: And he said it's not surprising that we're hearing more about charges than successful convictions, because it's tricky to prosecute and determine whether people deliberately voted when they shouldn't have.
occurrences.speaker: David Becker
occurrences.subject: U.S. Department of Justice
